messages:
alyssa (cs): Hey team — Acme (acct_acme_88) flagged a month-end mismatch. Dashboard shows 11,328,142 tokens for Feb but invoice total tokens = 18,056,760 and they were bumped a tier. Can someone triage? Invoice INV-2026-02-ACME. Attaching a few sample request_ids they pasted: rq_9f3a, rq_9f3b, rq_9f3c
matt (billing): Thanks. Do we have the invoice line items? Need plan id, lines, and the raw meter hash if available. Also any export from the usage API would help.
alyssa (cs): Paste of invoice lines (copied from billing UI):
- plan: pro-monthly (plan_id:pro_03) base included tokens: 5,000,000
- overage: 6,728,618 tokens @ $0.0002 = $1,345.72
- embeddings add-on: 5,328,142 tokens @ $0.0006 = $3,196.88
Total tokens: 18,056,760
Link to dashboard snapshot (private): https://redwood.internal/snapshots/acme/feb
matt (billing): Hmm embeddings add-on line looks suspicious — dashboard doesn't break out embeddings like that for Acme. Sophie / eng can you run a quick usage export for acct_acme_88 for Feb and share counts partitioned by api_type (generation/chat/embeddings)?
sophie (eng): On it. Quick note: common causes — duplicate ingestion, client retries that replay events, or a backfill job pulling historical events into the billing pipeline. Requesting raw event dump. Running internal query now:
```
SELECT api_type, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id='acct_acme_88' AND date >= '2026-02-01' AND date < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY api_type;
```
I'll paste results when ready.
samir (sre): I see a spike on 2026-02-28 23:40-23:55 UTC from that account in platform logs — lots of 5xx followed by client retries from the same IP range. Possible replay. Grabbing request traces for rq_9f3a/rq_9f3b.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-02-ACME generated at 2026-03-01T02:10:05Z, meter_hash: mtr_0a7c. Raw metering file: s3://billing-prod/metering/2026/02/INV-2026-02-ACME.csv
sophie (eng): Raw query result (summarized):
- chat/generation: 6,000,501 tokens
- embeddings: 11,327,759 tokens
Total: 17,328,260 tokens (slightly different from invoice due to rounding & meter file join).
Observation: embeddings count in usage export roughly equals the dashboard embeddings + an ~6M spike in the last day.
alyssa (cs): Acme replied — they ran a nightly backfill on 2026-02-28 that replayed events to our ingestion endpoint to fix their own analytics. They didn't realize it would hit our billing pipeline.
matt (billing): That explains it. Need to know whether those backfilled events were double-billed (i.e., original events already billed) or legitimately new. If duplicates, we should credit them. Can eng produce a dedupe key set (event_id/request_id) and a list we can use to reconcile meter file?
sophie (eng): Yes. Plan: 1) run dedupe script against s3://billing-prod/metering/2026/02/ to flag events with duplicate event_id or exact request payload hashes, 2) produce adjusted token totals, 3) create credit memo if duplicates > X tokens. Quick example of log pattern indicating duplicate:
```
2026-02-28T23:45:12Z acct_acme_88 rq_9f3a 500 "internal error"
2026-02-28T23:45:13Z acct_acme_88 rq_9f3a 200 "ok" (retry)
```
I can run the dedupe job and push results to /tmp/acme_dedupe_report.csv by EOD UTC.
samir (sre): Also recommend checking SDK version from customer — older SDKs retried on 5xx without idempotency. If they used that, many identical requests will appear. I can check headers for `x-client-sdk` in the traces.
matt (billing): OK — if script shows >100k duplicate tokens, we credit automatically. >1M tokens needs manager review. Keep me posted. Please hold invoice settlement for Acme until we confirm.
alyssa (cs): Noted — told customer we'll pause settlement and investigate. They're amenable to a credit if duplicates are confirmed. Thanks Sophie/Samir.
matt (billing): Assigning billing-ops to open a hold on INV-2026-02-ACME and tag with meter_hash mtr_0a7c. Will draft credit memo template once dedupe report lands.
alyssa (cs): Thanks — I'll update Acme and ask them for the backfill job logs (job_id, timeframe).
matt (billing): :thumbsup:
